chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Sy Oliver's role in shaping the Lunceford style
summary: Crawford says Sy Oliver contributed more to the Lunceford style than anyone, writing simple arrangements with a beat.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Now, I was going to say, now, Sy Oliver, we didn't talk about Sy Oliver. Now, do you -- I wanted to ask you something. There's some argument that goes on between different people about where the style of the Lunceford band came from. Some people say it came from Sy Oliver.
That's right. We had other arrangers
in there, such as Roger Seguerie and people like that. They were ofay boys. But Sy Oliver, technically speaking, contributed -- you going to read or listen?

He contributed more to the Lunceford style than anybody. We didn't have no style prior to Sy Oliver joining the band. But when Sy got there, he made sure you played his arrangements the way he wanted them. And -- which was a great thing. He contributed a great deal to that band.
Did you all have to rehearse? Was his music hard to play?

No, it was simple, but it had to be right, though. Sy wrote simply, even the things he went over there and did with Tommy Dorsey, when he started writing for Dorsey, after he left the band. Sy wrote simple, but he wrote with a beat. That bum could really write.

I mean, he was self-educated. He never had a lesson in arranging in his life. He just -- people had a piano, so he sat down and taught himself how to arrange. He was a pretty brilliant, bigheaded guy.
